args.text:
These are the duties of this job at the GS-12. If you're picked at a lower grade level, you'll get the chance to learn to do all of these duties, and you'll get training to help you grow in the job.

As a TECHNICAL WRITER-EDITOR, you will:

Properly handle the contents of documents and of Federal Register publications so they're published in a legally effective, timely and accurate way.

Manage work, whether you're doing it on your own, as part of a team, or leading others, so that all documents are published on time and accurately, and all program goals are met.

Understand and properly deal with customer needs across every part of the Federal Register publication process, in carrying out the Office of the Federal Register's program responsibilities.

Understand and properly use the technical resources available for, and tied to, the Federal Register publication processes, including information technology, legacy systems and other technical resources.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

This opportunity is also open to Status Candidates under Announcement ST-12632063-25-SW.

Please check that announcement for details on the open period, who's eligible, and how to apply.

The experience can have been gained in the public sector, the private sector or volunteer work. One year of experience means full-time work; part-time work is counted pro rata. To make sure you get full credit for your work experience, please show your dates of employment as month/day/year, and show the number of hours you worked each week, on your resume.

A one-year probation period may be required.

You must get through a background check.

Fill in a Declaration for Federal Employment, when the agency asks for it, so they can decide whether you're suitable for Federal employment.

If you're a male applicant born after 31 December 1959, certify that you've registered with the Selective Service System or are exempt from having to.

Go through a Personal Identity Verification (PIV) process that needs two forms of ID from the Form i-9. Federal law requires the identity and employment eligibility of all new starters in the U.S. to be verified.

Please see "Conditions of Employment."

Click "Print Preview" to read the whole announcement before you apply.

Must be U.S. Citizens or U.S. Nationals.

Qualifications

You must meet the following requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

Specialised Experience: For the GS-09, you must have one year of specialised experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equal to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service. Specialised experience for this job includes:

Editing legal or regulatory documents written by others to make sure they stick to style and formatting requirements before they're prepared for publication; AND

Spotting and analysing production problems and working out solutions to them; AND

Getting information across effectively and diplomatically to internal and/or external audiences in support of program goals.

OR

EDUCATION: A master's or equivalent graduate degree, or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree, or an LL.B. or J.D., if related.

OR

COMBINATION OF EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Note: Only graduate study beyond the first year (18 semester hours) counts towards qualifying for the GS-9.

NOTE: Undergraduate and Graduate Education: Must have included a total of 15 semester hours in a relevant scientific, technical or social science field (or fields), and at least one course above introductory level in the field (or fields) the job covers. For writers or editors of technical manuals and specifications, the equivalent of 15 semester hours can have been gained through vocational or educational training above high school level at a public, private or Armed Forces school.

Additional information

We may pick from this announcement or any other source to fill one or more vacancies.

This announcement may be used to fill similar jobs in other organisations within the National Archives and Records Administration.

This is a bargaining unit position, AFGE Council 260.

We offer the chance to work from home, per Agency policy.

We offer the chance of alternative and flexible work hours, per Agency policy.
